risk_of_bias.domain: liberal type I error rate / statistical power
risk_of_bias.judgement: The study was designed to yield 80% power at a two-sided-unspecified α = .20 significance level for a single dose comparison (4500 mg vs placebo), a far more permissive threshold than conventional α = .05, and the document describes no multiplicity control across the three dose arms and multiple endpoints.
risk_of_bias.quote: a standard deviation of 2.0 across participants, and a 25% dropout rate, this study was expected to yield 80% power at the α = .20 level

risk_of_bias.judgement: 19% of participants discontinued during the blinded portion of the study, and 35 of 457 randomized participants were not included in the mITT efficacy cohort (457 randomized, 422 analysed); the document states discontinuation was similar across treatment arms.
risk_of_bias.quote: The overall discontinuation rate during the blinded portion of the study was 19% and was similar across treatment arms.

risk_of_bias.domain: COVID-19 disruption of exposure and assessment
risk_of_bias.judgement: 72 participants missed 112 planned doses, and CDR, ADCS-ADL and A-IADL-Q were administered telephonically for 13% of week-69 and 16% of week-73 CDRs, introducing exposure and measurement heterogeneity that sensitivity analyses could only partly address.
risk_of_bias.quote: Owing to the COVID-19 pandemic, 72 participants missed a total of 112 planned doses between March 2020 and the end of the blinded period.

risk_of_bias.domain: internal numerical inconsistency between abstract and Table 2
risk_of_bias.judgement: The abstract reports adverse event counts that equal the arm denominators (placebo 130 [93.1%]; 4500 mg 132 [94.7%]; 8100 mg 90 [92.2%]) whereas Table 2 reports 121 (93.1%), 124 (93.9%) and 83 (92.2%); the counts and one percentage disagree between the two locations.
risk_of_bias.quote: similar proportions of participants experienced adverse events in the placebo (130 [93.1%]) and semorinemab (1500 mg: 89 [88.8%]; 4500 mg: 132 [94.7%]; 8100 mg: 90 [92.2%]) arms.

risk_of_bias.domain: sponsor involvement in conduct and analysis
risk_of_bias.judgement: The document refers to the sponsor as a blinded party to treatment allocation and describes the preclinical work supporting semorinemab as the authors' own ('Our preclinical studies'), but the retrieved text contains no funding statement or conflict-of-interest disclosure.
risk_of_bias.quote: Participants, investigators, and the sponsor were blinded to treatment allocation.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Of 422 participants in the mITT cohort, 388 (91.9%) were White, which the document itself flags as restricting generalizability.
risk_of_bias.quote: Of 422 individuals, 388 (91.9%) were White, and other individuals were American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, Black or African American, Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander, multiple race and ethnicity, or unknown.

disagreements.question: Does semorinemab slow clinical decline or cerebral tau accumulation in prodromal to mild Alzheimer disease?
disagreements.position: It does not. Semorinemab failed to demonstrate meaningful efficacy on clinical end points or reduction of tau accumulation across 18 months at the doses administered, and the authors present this as a negative result rather than an inconclusive one.
disagreements.attributed_to: Teng et al., the Tauriel investigators (this document)
disagreements.quote: these data indicate that semorinemab failed to demonstrate meaningful efficacy on clinical end points or reduction of tau accumulation across 18 months in participants with prodromal to mild AD at the doses administered

disagreements.question: Was the null result attributable to insufficient disease progression in the trial population?
disagreements.position: No. Decline on CDR-SB and tau PET accumulation were comparable with prior reports, so failure to detect a treatment effect was not due to insufficient progression.
disagreements.attributed_to: Teng et al., the Tauriel investigators (this document)
disagreements.quote: Taken together, these data suggest that the failure to detect treatment effects with semorinemab was not attributable to insufficient disease progression.

disagreements.question: Do these results refute the tau-spreading hypothesis of AD pathogenesis?
disagreements.position: The authors explicitly decline to draw that conclusion, stating their results do not directly address the validity of the tau-spreading hypothesis.
disagreements.attributed_to: Teng et al., the Tauriel investigators (this document)
disagreements.quote: Given the continued accumulation of tau pathology (as measured by tau PET) in the semorinemab dose arms, our results do not directly address the validity of the tau-spreading hypothesis of AD pathogenesis.

disagreements.question: Why did preclinical efficacy of the murine surrogate not translate to the clinic?
disagreements.position: The document offers several unresolved explanations, including that the N-terminal tau epitope semorinemab recognises may not be present in the tau species responsible for spread, and that tau may spread by membrane-enclosed mechanisms that preclude antibody clearance.
disagreements.attributed_to: Teng et al., the Tauriel investigators (this document)
disagreements.quote: One possibility is that the N -terminal tau epitope recognized by semorinemab is not present in the tau species that are primarily responsible for tau spread in prodromal to mild AD.

disagreements.question: Are other N-terminal anti-tau antibodies effective in analogous populations?
disagreements.position: The document reports that similarly negative results for gosuranemab and tilavonemab in analogous patient populations have recently been announced, while maintaining that tau remains a compelling therapeutic target.
disagreements.attributed_to: Teng et al., the Tauriel investigators (this document)
disagreements.quote: although similarly negative results of other N -terminal anti-tau antibodies (gosuranemab, tilavonemab) in analogous patient populations have recently been announced
